# Programs 6 internships (4 for summer 2027, 2 for January 2027), plus a Summer Leadership Program that isn't an internship


*Last updated: November 2026*


Wolf & Company has six internships open right now, and every one states its pay: $26.00 an hour. On October 12, 2026, the Boston firm's[job board](https://career-portal-wolfandco.icims.com/jobs/search?ss=1) listed **four summer 2027 internships** (assurance, corporate tax, internal audit and technology advisory) and **two January 2027 internships** (winter tax, and outsourced finance and accounting). University career boards that carry the same postings show recruiting began on September 11, 2026.


In plain words: you apply in fall 2026, and you intern either from January to April 2027 or in summer 2027. No posting states a deadline. The firm says its internships are for rising seniors, and it runs a separate Summer Leadership Program for rising sophomores and juniors, which isn't an internship.


---


## What Is a Wolf & Company Internship?


A Wolf & Company internship is a paid student role at Wolf & Company, P.C., a Boston accounting and advisory firm, in assurance, tax, internal audit, technology advisory or outsourced accounting. Interns join one department and work on client engagements with its staff. The firm's postings describe it as "one of the top 100 largest accounting firms in the United States" and "the fourth largest in New England," with more than 400 people. Its[about page](https://www.wolfandco.com/about/) traces the firm to 1911, when it started in Boston as Edwin L. Pride & Company.


Vault ranks Wolf & Company #42 on its[Most Prestigious Accounting Firms list](https://vault.com/best-companies-to-work-for/accounting/most-prestigious-accounting-firms) (2027 Vault Rankings). The[careers page](https://www.wolfandco.com/careers/) says internships are offered "across the firm for rising seniors" and that the firm's "hire-to-retire philosophy begins with our intern program." A separate Summer Leadership Program introduces rising sophomores and juniors to the profession. It's a short program for younger students, not an internship.


## When Do Wolf & Company Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


Wolf & Company posted its January 2027 and summer 2027 internships together. Career boards at Suffolk, MIT and the University of Rhode Island all show "Recruitment began on September 11, 2026" for these roles. That's about nine months before a summer 2027 start and about four months before the January 2027 start. On October 12, 2026, all six were still live on the firm's own board. We couldn't find posting dates for the summer 2026 cycle, so the expected window for summer 2028 (around September 2027) is projected from this one cycle and is low confidence.

*How to read this page: our dates come from tracking previous recruiting cycles and daily posting data. Treat them as informed estimates based on historical patterns, not confirmed dates. The company's official careers page is always the most current source. If a role is posted there, go by that, even if this page suggests the window hasn't opened yet.*


### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


Wolf & Company's postings behave like rolling ones. None of the six states a deadline, a closing date or a review date, and all six were still accepting applications on October 12, 2026, a month after they went up. That isn't a reason to wait. Each posting covers one department in one office, at a firm of a bit more than 400 people, so don't expect a large class.


The January 2027 cohort is the tighter one. Winter tax interns start in about three months, so that posting has the least time left. One date to ignore: campus career boards show these listings expiring on October 12, 2026. That's the same one-month listing period at all three schools we checked, and it isn't a deadline set by the firm. Go by the firm's own board.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


The six postings ask for less than most firms' do. Here is what they state and what they leave out:


• **Enrollment:** five postings say you must "currently be enrolled at a college or university"; the outsourced accounting posting says "currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree."


• **Class year:** the firm's careers page says internships are for rising seniors. The postings themselves don't name a class year, and the outsourced accounting role lists junior or senior standing as preferred.


• **Major:** each posting names its degrees. Corporate tax and winter tax want accounting. Assurance is the broadest. Technology advisory wants information systems or cyber security students.


• **GPA:** no posting states a minimum. The outsourced accounting role asks for introductory accounting coursework "with a strong academic record."


• **Work authorization:** not addressed in any of the six postings.


• **Location:** all six are in Boston.


### Is There a GPA Cutoff at Wolf & Company?


Not a published one. None of the six postings names a GPA, which is unusual for an accounting firm. Don't read that as no screen at all: the firm doesn't say how it reviews transcripts, and one posting asks for a strong academic record. The class-year question matters more. The careers page pitches internships at rising seniors, while the postings only require enrollment. If you're a sophomore or junior, apply if you fit the posting, and ask the recruiter about the Summer Leadership Program too.

## What Skills Does Wolf & Company Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


Wolf & Company's postings are short, and they repeat the same four soft skills almost word for word: strong **oral and written communication** , **presentation skills** , **analytical skills** and being "very well organized." The technical asks come from the work itself. Assurance interns audit financial statements and see SOC attestation reporting. Internal audit and technology advisory interns both **test controls** , one on business processes and the other on networks, applications and security. The two tax roles cover planning and compliance. Only the outsourced accounting posting names a tool: **Microsoft Excel** , alongside cloud accounting platforms.

## What Is the Wolf & Company Application and Interview Process Like?


Wolf & Company doesn't publish its interview process, and we found no candidate accounts of it. Here is what the board and careers page show:


1. **Pick one department.** Each posting is tied to one department and one season, so choose by your degree and by whether you can work full-time from January to April.


2. **Apply on the job board.** Every posting has its own Apply button, and you create a candidate login on the board.


3. **Use your campus channel if you have one.** The firm pushed these listings to career boards at Suffolk, MIT and the University of Rhode Island on the day recruiting began, and it has an employer page on Handshake.


4. **Interviews.** The number of rounds and the format aren't published anywhere we could find. Prepare for behavioral questions and for a conversation about why this department.


5. **Start.** The January 2027 cohort starts in January; summer 2027 interns are expected to start around June.


Because the format isn't published, practice the general case. Our[behavioral interview guide](https://www.extern.com/post/behavioral-interview-questions-star-method-guide) covers the question types most accounting firms use.


### What the Community Says


We found no Reddit thread and no readable intern review about Wolf & Company internships, so there are no community cards here. Searches for the firm mostly return a Chicago cafe with the same name. The firm has an employer page on Handshake, where reviews sit behind a student login, so your own school's Handshake is the best place to look for first-hand accounts.


## How Do You Stand Out for a Wolf & Company Internship?


Three moves. **First, match your degree to the posting.** Each one names its majors. Corporate tax and winter tax ask for accounting, assurance takes business, economics, finance and information systems too, and technology advisory is for information systems or cyber security students. **Second, show the four skills every posting repeats.** Communication, presentation, analysis and organization appear almost word for word across the board, so bring one example of each, such as a class presentation or a club budget you kept. **Third, know the client base.** The postings name financial institutions first among the industries the firm serves, along with manufacturing, investment advisors, and software and technology. Say which one interests you and why.


Wolf & Company publishes no applicant count, class size or conversion rate. What it does say is that its "hire-to-retire philosophy begins with our intern program," and seven entry-level staff roles sit on the same board as the internships.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Wolf & Company internship?


No. Summer 2026 has passed, and no summer 2026 posting is on the firm's board. What's open now is the next cycle: four summer 2027 internships in assurance, corporate tax, internal audit and technology advisory, plus two January 2027 internships in winter tax and outsourced finance and accounting. All six are in Boston.


### When do Wolf & Company internship applications open for summer 2027?


They're already open. University career boards show recruiting for the summer 2027 and January 2027 internships began on September 11, 2026, and all six postings were live on October 12, 2026. For summer 2028, expect postings around September 2027. That estimate comes from one documented cycle, so treat it as low confidence.


### Is there a deadline for Wolf & Company internships?


None is stated. All six postings for January 2027 and summer 2027 are silent on closing dates, and they were still open a month after posting. Campus career boards show an October 12, 2026 expiry, but that's the boards' own one-month listing period. Apply soon anyway, because each posting covers a single department in one office.


### How much do Wolf & Company interns make?


$26.00 an hour. Each of the six postings for January 2027 and summer 2027 says "The salary for this position is $26.00 per hour," so the rate is the same in assurance, tax, internal audit, technology advisory and outsourced accounting. The postings don't mention housing, a signing bonus or overtime terms for interns.


### Who is eligible for a Wolf & Company internship?


Students currently enrolled in college with the degree a posting names. The firm's careers page says internships are for rising seniors, though the postings don't state a class year, a GPA minimum or a work authorization rule. Rising sophomores and juniors can look at the Summer Leadership Program, which is separate and isn't an internship.


### What internships does Wolf & Company offer?


Six, as of October 12, 2026. For summer 2027: assurance, corporate tax, internal audit and technology advisory. For January 2027: a full-time winter tax internship that runs January to April, and an outsourced finance and accounting internship over the same months. Each is a separate posting, so you apply to one department at a time.


### Where are Wolf & Company internships located?


All six open internships are in Boston, the firm's headquarters. Its job board lists other locations, including Springfield, Albany, New York City and Tampa, but no internship was tagged to them on October 12, 2026. The outsourced accounting posting expects at least one day a week in the Boston office; the others don't describe a hybrid schedule.


### Do Wolf & Company interns get full-time offers?


The firm doesn't publish a conversion rate. Its careers page says its "hire-to-retire philosophy begins with our intern program," and it features a video titled "From Intern to Principal." Seven entry-level staff roles are posted on the same board as the internships, in the same departments, so the internship is a visible route in.


Wolf & Company's six internships are open with no stated deadline, so pick your department and apply. Then add proof: a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) gives you a finished finance, data or security project to talk through in your interview.
